propositions: Core push implementation executes five CAS retry cycles with push-first, fetch-and-merge recovery only after retriable rejection, followed by exactly one conditional terminal push if the fifth rejection produces a clean merge.

Strict delivery is opt-in via keyword-only parameter, raises catchable PushDeliveryError with machine-stable reasons and unpushed-commit detail, and is translated to stderr plus nonzero exit only by the Python module adapter.

All pre-existing callers (event append, batch append, NDJSON import, transition close, delete, compact, claim) retain best-effort default behavior and inherit the corrected five-cycle retry budget without strict opt-in.
Strict delivery writes no ticket event, emits no BRIDGE_ALERT, and preserves working-tree and HEAD state; best-effort paired controls remain unchanged.
Policy-decline rejections (branch protection) map to push-policy-declined while transport failures map to push-transport-failed, preserving the distinction established in prior operational guidance.
